business_patterns.top_pattern: DSNP and SNP claims in the Not Mapped facility bucket are the largest spend driver
business_patterns.what_is_impacting: DSNP HMO and SNP Crossover / Not Mapped facility claims
business_patterns.pattern_details: A very large share of the increase is sitting in the Not Mapped facility bucket, led by IN DSNP HMO and supported by smaller but similar spikes in TX, CA, CO, and TX SNP Crossover. Because the claims are not tied to a usable facility category, the current result blends utilization, site-of-care, and reimbursement effects. This should be treated as a gating validation issue before broad authorization, network, or pricing action is taken.
business_patterns.why_it_matters: This is the single largest pattern and can misdirect both utilization management and provider action if the claims are not first assigned to the right facility bucket.
business_patterns.recommended_next_step: Run a focused claims-mapping correction for Not Mapped facility claims in IN DSNP HMO first, then TX/CA/CO DSNP HMO and TX SNP Crossover, and only then re-run provider and site-of-care action planning.
business_patterns.validation_reason: Facility attribution is missing on the main claims driving the increase, so root-cause attribution is not reliable until mapping is corrected.
evidence_summary: IN DSNP HMO Not Mapped claims increased by +$50.5M across 94,559 claims, with paid per admit up about $192.
CA/CO/TX DSNP HMO Not Mapped claims added +$3.7M, with TX contributing +$3.6M and 7,082 more claims.
TX SNP Crossover Not Mapped claims added another +$675K across 5,458 claims.
All contributing groups were flagged for unmapped or unknown values and repeated concentration.

business_patterns.top_pattern: Large unattributed outpatient spend is concentrated in temporary-code and not-mapped categories
business_patterns.what_is_impacting: UNATTRIBUTED / OP HH/DME and OP Mgmt Oth Misc
business_patterns.pattern_details: A large unattributed outpatient increase is concentrated in OP HH/DME and OP Mgmt Oth Misc, tied to R69 and temporary or national code groupings. The mix of unattributed claims, not-mapped categories, and temporary codes makes this look more like coding, classification, or feed drift than a clean utilization trend. Validate attribution and code mapping before changing outpatient authorization rules.
business_patterns.why_it_matters: This is the second-largest dollar pattern and could drive the wrong outpatient policy response if it is treated as true utilization growth.
business_patterns.recommended_next_step: Audit the UNATTRIBUTED outpatient feed for R69, temporary national codes, and national T codes; correct attribution and benefit mapping, then reassess whether any real utilization or unit-cost issue remains.
business_patterns.validation_reason: The increase is concentrated in unattributed claims and temporary or not-mapped outpatient coding, so business action should wait for coding and attribution cleanup.
evidence_summary: UNATTRIBUTED OP HH/DME increased by +$25.4M across 32,835 claims, tied to R69 and Temporary National Codes (Non-Medicare).
UNATTRIBUTED OP Mgmt Oth Misc added +$16.9M across 47,830 claims, split between Temporary National Codes (Non-Medicare) and National T Codes.
Both groups were flagged for not-mapped values, repeated concentration, and low-baseline behavior.
The pattern is concentrated enough to warrant data cleanup before operational action.

business_patterns.top_pattern: Post-acute spend is rising, led by Indiana home health with smaller SNF and NF outliers
business_patterns.what_is_impacting: DSNP HMO / Home Health, SNF, and NF post-acute services
business_patterns.pattern_details: Post-acute pressure is being driven mainly by Indiana DSNP home health, with smaller skilled nursing and nursing facility outlier cases across IN, TX, and VA. This points to a site-of-care and provider-mix issue in post-acute services rather than a broad acute inpatient trend. The main business levers are authorization pathway design, discharge steering, and provider rate review in post-acute settings.
business_patterns.why_it_matters: Post-acute placement decisions can scale quickly, so early action on home health and skilled nursing can prevent a broader cost trend.
business_patterns.recommended_next_step: Review DSNP post-acute authorization and discharge pathways in IN first, then validate provider-specific SNF and NF outliers in TX and IN for placement appropriateness and contracted rate accuracy.
evidence_summary: IN DSNP HMO home health increased by +$5.4M across 8,268 claims, with paid per admit up about $635.
DSNP HMO SNF claims across IN/TX/VA added +$72K, concentrated at PROVENA SACRED HEART HOME and THE RENAISSANCE AT KESSLER PARK.
NF rare cases across IN/TX added +$72K, led by Organic Disturbances and Intellectual Disability, Osteomyelitis with MCC, and Pulmonary Edema and Respiratory Failure.
The smaller SNF and NF signals are low volume, but they support the broader post-acute concentration story.

business_patterns.top_pattern: Texas DSNP acute hospital spend is rising mainly on price, with rare inpatient cases adding pressure
business_patterns.what_is_impacting: TX / DSNP HMO / Acute Hospital and IP Med/Surg
key_driver_codes: Disorders of the Biliary Tract with MCC
Other O.R. Procedures for Multiple Significant Trauma with MCC
business_patterns.pattern_details: Texas DSNP acute hospital pressure is primarily reimbursement or unit-cost driven, not broad volume growth. The core acute hospital increase is material even with slightly lower claim volume, and a small number of expensive IP Med/Surg admissions are adding to the total. This supports immediate pricing and case-management action in TX acute facilities.
business_patterns.why_it_matters: This is the largest mapped inpatient pressure outside the validation buckets and gives a direct contract and inpatient management lever in Texas.
business_patterns.recommended_next_step: Audit TX DSNP acute hospital reimbursement and contract terms, and pair that with case-level review of the listed high-cost biliary, esophageal, GI obstruction, and trauma admissions.
evidence_summary: TX DSNP HMO acute hospital unit-cost pressure added +$3.0M while claim count fell by 208 and paid per admit rose about $3,827.
Additional TX DSNP acute hospital mixed pressure added +$756K across four high-cost DRGs.
TX IP Med/Surg rare cases added +$620K, largely from one-claim admissions in biliary, esophageal, and GI obstruction categories.
Several supporting admissions were paid at roughly $173K to $222K per admit.

business_patterns.top_pattern: Ohio acute hospital growth is concentrated in two DSNP providers
business_patterns.what_is_impacting: OH / DSNP HMO / Acute Hospital providers

providers: MERCY HEALTH- SAINT VINCENT MEDICAL CENTER

key_driver_codes: MERCY HEALTH- SAINT VINCENT MEDICAL CENTER
Septicemia or Severe Sepsis with Mechanical Ventilation >96 Hours
business_patterns.pattern_details: Ohio DSNP acute hospital spend is concentrated at MIAMI VALLEY HOSPITAL and MERCY HEALTH- SAINT VINCENT MEDICAL CENTER, where both utilization and paid per admission are rising. Supporting inpatient outlier cases at the same providers reinforce a provider-specific economics story rather than a statewide issue. This is best handled through targeted provider review, not a broad product rule change.
business_patterns.why_it_matters: Concentration at two facilities creates a faster and more actionable savings lever than a broad statewide intervention.
business_patterns.recommended_next_step: Launch provider-level contract and case-management review for MIAMI VALLEY HOSPITAL and MERCY HEALTH- SAINT VINCENT MEDICAL CENTER, including admission and payment review on the identified inpatient DRGs.
business_patterns.validation_reason: The increase is highly concentrated in a few providers and low-volume inpatient cases, so confirm case mix and payment accuracy before broad network action.
evidence_summary: MIAMI VALLEY HOSPITAL increased by +$827K across 507 claims, with paid per admit up about $1,632.
MERCY HEALTH- SAINT VINCENT MEDICAL CENTER added +$370K across 61 claims, with paid per admit up about $6,072.
Supporting OH and UNATTRIBUTED IP Med/Surg outliers added +$296K, including sepsis and infectious-disease surgical cases at the same providers.
The pattern is concentrated enough for provider-specific intervention.

business_patterns.top_pattern: California acute inpatient cost growth is being driven by rare high-cost trauma and surgical cases
business_patterns.what_is_impacting: CA / DSNP HMO / Acute Hospital and IP Med/Surg

providers: EL CAMINO HEALTH - MOUNTAIN VIEW HOSPITAL

key_driver_codes: EL CAMINO HEALTH - MOUNTAIN VIEW HOSPITAL
Other O.R. Procedures for Multiple Significant Trauma with MCC
Disorders of the Biliary Tract with MCC
business_patterns.pattern_details: California acute inpatient pressure is being driven by a narrow set of rare, very expensive trauma and surgical admissions, with added concentration at EL CAMINO HEALTH - MOUNTAIN VIEW HOSPITAL. This is an outlier-case pattern, not broad inpatient growth. The right response is case-level review, payment validation, and targeted provider discussion rather than population-wide utilization controls.
business_patterns.why_it_matters: Rare catastrophic inpatient cases can materially move spend even at low volume, so they need a different playbook than broad utilization trends.
business_patterns.recommended_next_step: Send the listed trauma and surgical admissions for case-level clinical and payment review, and validate outlier reimbursement terms with EL CAMINO HEALTH - MOUNTAIN VIEW HOSPITAL.
business_patterns.validation_reason: The increase is driven by a handful of one- to three-claim admissions, so coding and payment accuracy should be confirmed before broader action.
evidence_summary: CA DSNP acute hospital pressure added +$839K, including +$431K at EL CAMINO HEALTH - MOUNTAIN VIEW HOSPITAL.
CA IP Med/Surg rare cases added +$864K across five single-case trauma diagnoses.
The trauma DRG alone added +$388K in the acute hospital view.
Several individual admissions were paid between about $90K and $254K per admit.

business_patterns.top_pattern: Outpatient oncology and chemotherapy claims show a small but distinct mapping issue
business_patterns.what_is_impacting: CA / OH / OP IV Therapy-Oncology and OP Mgmt Oth Misc chemotherapy

providers: EL CAMINO HEALTH - MOUNTAIN VIEW HOSPITAL
MERCY HEALTH- SAINT VINCENT MEDICAL CENTER

business_patterns.pattern_details: A small but recurring set of outpatient oncology and chemotherapy claims is appearing in CA and OH, with claims landing in not-mapped outpatient groupings. The dollars are modest, but oncology is a distinct pathway and should not be folded into general outpatient validation. Confirm chemotherapy coding and benefit assignment before any oncology authorization changes are considered.
business_patterns.why_it_matters: Even small oncology misclassification can create the wrong medical-versus-pharmacy policy response.
business_patterns.recommended_next_step: Have clinical and data-quality teams validate chemotherapy drug coding, regimen classification, and benefit assignment for the named providers before adjusting oncology authorization rules.
business_patterns.validation_reason: The pattern depends on chemotherapy claims landing in not-mapped outpatient groupings, so coding and benefit mapping must be checked first.
evidence_summary: CA/OH OP IV Therapy-Oncology added +$69K from four claims across EL CAMINO HEALTH - MOUNTAIN VIEW HOSPITAL and MERCY HEALTH- SAINT VINCENT MEDICAL CENTER.
CA OP Mgmt Oth Misc chemotherapy added +$59K from three claims at EL CAMINO HEALTH - MOUNTAIN VIEW HOSPITAL.
All supporting claims involved Chemotherapy Drugs and not-mapped outpatient grouping.
This is low volume but clinically distinct enough to warrant separate oncology validation.

business_patterns.top_pattern: Medicare HMO acute hospital increases are emerging in CO, IN, and CA but remain low volume
key_driver_codes: Other O.R. Procedures for Multiple Significant Trauma with MCC
business_patterns.pattern_details: Medicare HMO acute hospital increases are present in CO, IN, and CA, but each market is small and case-driven. This looks like emerging pressure from a few admissions rather than a broad product-wide trend. Use targeted case and payment review, but do not treat it as a systemic utilization issue yet.
business_patterns.why_it_matters: Early case-level review can prevent a small acute pattern from growing into a broader Medicare HMO cost issue.
business_patterns.recommended_next_step: Run focused case and payment audits on the identified CO, IN, and CA Medicare HMO acute admissions before considering any broader product or network changes.
business_patterns.validation_reason: Most of the increase is driven by a small number of admissions, so payment and case classification should be confirmed before broader action.
evidence_summary: CO Medicare HMO acute hospital spend increased by +$333K across 222 claims, with paid per admit up about $575.
IN Medicare HMO acute hospital added +$254K from a single trauma admission.
CA Medicare HMO acute hospital added +$43K from two major esophageal disorder admissions.
The combined signal is real but still too small and concentrated for a broad product response.

executive_summary.headline: The biggest cost story is not-mapped and unattributed claim concentration, with the clearest actionable provider-mix pressure sitting in TX, OH, CA, and IN.
executive_summary.primary_business_message: More than half of the identified increase is tied to claims that are either in Not Mapped facility buckets or unattributed outpatient categories, so validation has to come first. Once those issues are separated, the clearest business levers are Texas acute hospital pricing, Ohio provider concentration, California rare high-cost inpatient outliers, and Indiana-led post-acute growth.
recommended_focus_order: Fix Not Mapped and UNATTRIBUTED claim classification before broad policy action.
Act on mapped acute hospital pressure next: TX pricing, OH provider concentration, and CA rare high-cost inpatient cases.
Use targeted post-acute management in IN and validate oncology and low-volume Medicare HMO signals case by case.

notes: Operational Not Mapped groups were intentionally consolidated into one gating validation pattern because the same mapping issue appears across multiple segments and products.
UNATTRIBUTED outpatient groups were consolidated into one validation pattern because they share the same temporary-code and not-mapped business mechanism.
Several acute hospital patterns intentionally combine operational and clinical groups where the clinical cases explain the same downstream inpatient action.
All analytical groups were assigned to a business pattern.
Segment attribution is weak for 57% of cards (30 of 53) on segment_by [service_area_state]; add those dimensions to the stage's dimension or carry-through list to attribute them at cell level.
